title: Opportunistic partial-decode checkpoints and kernel-substitution for fragmented KV shards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: serving instances spend disproportionate time in full-token prefill/initial decode when a request touches multiple small fragmented KV shards. This causes two related costs: higher p95 prefill latency (tail spikes when multiple tiny fragments cause kernel warmups) and excessive KV churn/eviction because partial work writes back inconsistent residency information.

Goal: implement a two-part runtime optimization: (1) lightweight partial-decode checkpoints at shard boundaries so that interrupted or interleaved decodes can resume and reuse partially-computed KV state without forcing full re-prefill; (2) an opportunistic kernel-substitution layer that can choose lower-overhead kernels (small-block matmul / sparse-friendly paths) for fragments that meet density/shape heuristics to reduce per-fragment warmup cost. Both pieces should integrate with scheduling: prefer high-affinity ordering (group fragments by expected decode window and kernel affinity) to reduce context switches and KV thrashing.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end p95 prefill latency reduction >= 10% on mixed small-fragment workload (internal benchmark suite).
- KV writeback/reclamation events reduced by >= 20% on synthetic interleaved request traces.
- No regression (>1%) in average token throughput for standard dense workloads.
- Feature gated behind "partial_checkpointing" and "opportunistic_kernels" flags; controlled rollout via runtime-1.22.

Out of scope: global rebalancer work, long-term shard compaction algorithm; this ticket focuses on local checkpointing and kernel routing at runtime serving layer.
implementation_plan: Design checkpoint data structure and minimal serialization format (checkpoint contains descriptor of token-span, KV pointers, kernel-tag, decode-position).
Add a small in-memory checkpoint cache per-KV-shard with LRU eviction and soft TTL tied to request affinity windows.
Instrument fragment density heuristic: measure non-zero occupancy and token-span length; produce continuous score used by kernel-selector.
Implement kernel-substitution hooks in serving runtime: register alternate kernels with capabilities (small-block, sparse, fused-prefix).
Modify prefill scheduler to emit ordered decode tasks grouped by kernel-affinity and token-window to reduce context switches and increase burst reuse.
Expose runtime flags and per-tenant toggles in config; default off for experiments. Add telemetry counters for checkpoint hits/misses and kernel-substitutions.
design_notes: Checkpoint granularity: prefer shard-boundary points that map to contiguous kv-slot ranges; avoid per-token checkpoints to limit memory overhead.
Checkpoint format must be compact — expect ~200-600 bytes per checkpoint depending on model; plan for 32MB soft budget per GPU instance.
Kernel selector will be heuristics-first: density < 0.3 and token-span < 64 -> try small-block kernel; else use standard kernel. Measure and fallback on latency.
Scheduling heuristic: stable affinity ordering by predicted next-token-window reduces eviction pressure observed in traces collected from multi-tenant tests.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization/deserialization and backward compatibility with existing shard layout.
Integration tests: replay recorded interleaved traces from production-mimic bench (sourced from s3://redwood-bench/prefill-interleaved-2026-02).
Performance A/B in canary fleet: run 48-hour experiment comparing flags off vs both flags on; collect p50/p95/p99 prefill latency and KV churn metrics.
Chaos test: simulate mid-decode eviction and ensure resume from checkpoint does not produce inconsistent KV writes or double-count tokens.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike complete. Prototype checkpoint layout and a toy kernel-substitution shim. Benchmarks show 12% reduction in per-fragment warmup on synthetic microbench.
2026-03-04: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Feedback: checkpoint memory budget needs guardrails, prefer per-tenant soft caps. Action: add eviction quotas per-tenant.
2026-03-06: Implemented in-memory checkpoint cache and serializer. Added telemetry: checkpoint_put/checkpoint_hit/checkpoint_evict counters (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/12458).

2026-03-09: Early integration test failed in odd-multitenant trace due to kernel-tag mismatch on resume. Root cause: kernel ABI versioning not fully encoded in checkpoint — added kernel-tag + version into checkpoint descriptor.
2026-03-12: Re-ran interleaved bench: checkpoint hit rate ~18%, opportunistic kernel path used for ~22% of fragments; p95 prefill improved 11% on bench. Preparing canary rollout plan.
Reviewer notes (from SRE): ensure checkpoint garbage collection does not correlate with host OOM — recommend periodic sampling GC rather than synchronous on-alloc.
review_feedback: PM (R. Chen): prioritize safety toggles and per-tenant telemetry before canary and document expected memory costs in SLO runbooks.
Runtime lead (L. Gomez): prefer conservative default heuristics and require timing-based fallback if opportunistic kernel path exceeds 5ms overhead.
Design (E. Park): ensure resume semantics are idempotent for repeated retries and include strong checksums in checkpoint to avoid state corruption.
next_steps: Add per-tenant checkpoint soft-cap and eviction alarms (estimate 2 days).
Complete canary rollout with 5% traffic and monitor p95/p99 and KV_evict_count over 72h.
Prep runtime docs and Console feature flag UI entries; coordinate with product for release notes in runtime-1.22.
risks: Memory overhead if tenant workloads create many short-lived checkpoints — mitigated by soft caps and TTL-based GC.
Kernel-substitution may increase tail latency for some shapes; always measure and provide immediate fallback to stable kernel.
Checkpoint format changes may complicate cross-version resume in mixed-cluster upgrades — plan to gate resume on explicit compatibility flags.
